cta.heading: Senior design capacity this quarter, not after a long hire
cta.body: Tell us about your product and timeline. We usually suggest starting with a two-week UX audit, to test working together across the distance.

sections.heading: What US software teams tend to need

items.title: Accessibility is a litigation surface
items.body: ADA web accessibility claims run into the thousands each year and enterprise procurement increasingly asks for a VPAT. Designing to WCAG 2.1 AA from the start costs a fraction of retrofitting.

items.title: Senior design is expensive and slow to hire
items.body: For many teams the constraint is getting senior capacity onto the problem this quarter.

items.title: Enterprise buyers audit design maturity
items.body: Procurement reviews look at accessibility, consistency and documentation.

items.title: Offshore has burned you before
items.body: The usual failure is layers, not skill: account managers, juniors after the pitch, no overlap hours. We have made the opposite choices.

sections.heading: How we work with US teams

items.title: Time zones
items.body: A 9am to 1pm EST overlap window for live calls and reviews, earlier in our day for PST teams. Everything else runs async.

items.title: Async by default
items.body: Loom walkthroughs, structured written updates and Figma comments, so progress doesn't depend on both sides being awake.

items.title: Contracting
items.body: USD contracts, US-standard NDAs and full IP assignment on payment, with W-8BEN documentation provided.

items.title: Senior designers, directly
items.body: No account managers and no junior hand-off after the sale.

items.title: Accessibility documentation
items.body: WCAG 2.1 AA designed in, with the documentation enterprise procurement asks for.

items.title: Engineering-compatible handover
items.body: Specs against your stack, delivered in increments that match your release rhythm.

sections.heading: The honest trade-off
paras: We are an India-based studio that works with US teams remotely; we do not have a US office and would rather say so. You get senior designers directly and capacity in weeks rather than after a months-long hire. The trade-off is time zone, which async working and a defined overlap window address but do not eliminate. If you need someone in the room every day, hire locally.

faq.q: How do you handle the time difference with US teams?
faq.a: We keep a 9am to 1pm EST overlap window for live calls and reviews and run everything else async, through Loom walkthroughs, written updates and Figma comments. For PST teams the overlap shifts earlier in our day.

faq.q: Do you have a US office?
faq.a: No. We are an India-based studio that works with US teams remotely. What we offer is USD contracting, US-standard NDAs and IP assignment, EST/PST overlap hours and senior designers on your project.

faq.q: Do you design to ADA and WCAG standards?
faq.a: WCAG 2.1 AA is our default. In the US this matters commercially as well as ethically, because accessibility claims run into the thousands each year and enterprise procurement increasingly requires a VPAT.

faq.q: How do you handle IP, NDAs and contracting?
faq.a: US-standard NDAs, full IP assignment on payment, and USD contracts. We provide W-8BEN documentation so your finance team isn't navigating an unfamiliar process.
Design kickoff is normally within 48 hours of signature, with an initial direction typically within five working days.
